newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks plunge on renewed jitters.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks plunge on renewed jitters.

text.p: Brazilian stocks plunged 4.66 percent Friday on what appeared to be strong fund selling to cover anticipated withdrawals from retail investors next week, traders and analysts said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of 47 most-traded shares ended at 11182, following a week of losses set off by currency fears stemming from recent devaluations in Asian emerging markets.
The Dow's 130 point fall on Friday also weighed on local stocks, traders said.
Volume was heavy with 1.425 billion reais trading hands.
Analysts said small-time investors whose investments in mutual funds had helped push the market up over 90 percent this year through mid-July were now getting cold feet and want to take profits.
"Monday will be a very nervous day because that is when we will see what the fund redemptions are," said one broker, who said mutual fund redemptions on Tuesday alone totalled 250 million reais.
Benchmark Telebras preferred shares fell 4.67 percent to 140 on Friday.
Eletrobras was hammered with a 7.58 percent loss to 500. Fears a recent government decree over privatization rules could harm Eletrobras minority shareholders contributed to the loss, traders said.
Petrobras preferred held up better, falling 3.41 percent to 283.

The market's strong rally was checked by fears early this week that Asian currency turmoil could spread to Brazil. While the government and economists said such a scenario was unlikely, the market was seen looking for any excuse to take profits.
